shoal_e12_entry.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_entry.text: On Day Three Hundred Ten, Yue woke to a quieter harbor and a smell that had settled into cloth. The fire had not become safe because the visible flame was smaller. The night crew still held the guarded boundary around unstable hot debris. Her own support role had ended yesterday at its actual stop. Today began with the body condition that role had left, and with qualified workers whose night had continued after she slept.

shoal_e12_guide_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_guide_01.text: The guide role had left Yue ordinarily tired but without the relay's renewed fingertip change. She reported her current baseline to Yan when he checked the completed support count. Her old shoulder still allowed only its cleared waist work. She would not take a load job merely because yesterday's walking had been tolerable. Yan asked her to keep today's ordinary route outside hot debris and let the qualified entry crew do its own work.

shoal_e12_guide_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_guide_02.text: The four custodians had reached their offered storage through the safe long route. Eight owner-labeled bundles remained sealed under lawful keeper custody. Their internal condition review would occur only when the proper owners and a qualified ordinary reader could attend. The mould bay's burned stock remained inaccessible pending a separate inventory. Yesterday's exterior success was enough to establish receiving. It was not enough to certify every saved annotation or hide the other group's loss.

shoal_e12_guide_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_guide_03.text: One custodian wanted her drawing opened immediately because she had dreamed its ink was running. The keeper offered the current permitted review time and refused to break another owner's seal while waiting. She accepted her own appointment and left the remaining bundles untouched. Fear could make a saved object feel lost until seen again. Yue listened without promising an extra private opening from a custodian who did not own all eight pieces.

shoal_e12_guide_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_guide_04.text: The public support-care allowance had paid six copper for the strained-wrist helper's actual assessment and follow-up. Its second slot was unused under this route and six copper returned to the named source. Yue had not received a phantom pail injury or claimed that unused care payment as a reward. The helper's current restriction remained his own clinical information except for the work limit he chose to share with command.

shoal_e12_guide_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_guide_05.text: At the public wall, the mould worker who had wanted his stock saved declined conversation with Yue. He was waiting for the later inventory and did not want to hear another explanation of route feasibility. She respected the refusal. The drawings' owners could be relieved while he remained angry. A useful safe guide task did not grant its volunteer immunity from ordinary people's disappointment in the material result.

shoal_e12_guide_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_guide_06.text: She ate a proper breakfast before walking back to the safe boundary. The lodging keeper did not waive its rate because her coat smelled of smoke. Her received restoration wages and settled own savings covered the current agreement. A guide who had helped other people's property reach lawful storage still needed to pay for her own bed. The unexceptional expense made the harbor's morning feel solid beneath a night that had seemed unreal.

shoal_e12_guide_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_guide_07.text: The record custodian with the key came to thank the route hand who had refused the smoky shortcut. He accepted thanks for a completed instruction and said the actual long-route check had made it possible. He did not claim the cabinet was always destined to survive. Yue liked the ordinary answer. It preserved the choices of people who had walked, checked, waited, and opened a lawful lock under conditions that could have changed.

shoal_e12_guide_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_guide_08.text: At the guarded bay, qualified fire workers still had no safe entry to the mould remains. Its actual owners could request a later accompanied inventory, not cross the rope because they knew which piece had mattered most. Yue stood well back. The absence of a current count was painful, especially after an eight-bundle count had been available elsewhere. The fire had left different groups with different kinds of waiting.

shoal_e12_guide_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_guide_09.text: Yan asked whether she wanted another emergency assignment today. Yue said she had accepted yesterday's finite role and wanted only to attend the offered public updates. He found other actual willing helpers for the defined current tasks. Her refusal did not alter care access, earned stage, or friendships with these people. It kept the command's people list honest. She could help later through a separate offered task if her body and time actually allowed it.

shoal_e12_guide_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_guide_10.text: She returned to the public waiting area carrying no private drawings and no unresolved guide duty. The eight sealed bundles stood in keeper custody. The burned mould bay stood behind its qualified closure. The strained-wrist helper rested under his accepted plan, and unused support care had returned to its source. Yue could attend the larger containment account as an ordinary listener, with the actual material history of her chosen role still intact.

shoal_e12_relay_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_relay_01.text: The relay's renewed fingertip change remained on Day Three Hundred Ten's actual check. The ordinary practitioner tested touch, grip, and leg stability, asked about new symptoms, and kept Yue off load handling. Her shoulder's waist restriction also remained. This review belonged to the accepted six-copper assessment and follow-up slot. It did not draw again from the closed school account or promise that surviving moulds would make her body recover faster.

shoal_e12_relay_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_relay_02.text: The public support-care allowance had paid two actual six-copper assessment and follow-up scopes: the common strained-wrist helper and Yue's relay-related check. All twelve copper were used under the named source. No unused slot was returned through this route. The two bodies had different current limits, and the fire command needed only the applicable work restrictions they consented to share. Their private care details did not become an ordinary public inventory.

shoal_e12_relay_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_relay_03.text: At the mould cart, the owners could inspect exterior marks from the safe side while thirty provisionally working pieces and four visibly cracked pieces awaited qualified condition review. Yesterday's count had established material receiving, not thirty usable tools. Yue did not handle a piece to prove her fingers had recovered. Her contribution had ended on the relay's actual stop. The kept stock could wait for people whose current bodies and skills qualified its next movement.

shoal_e12_relay_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_relay_04.text: The record custodians' cabinet remained in the burned annex behind an unsafe approach. They had their lawful keys and no accessible bundles yet. One owner wanted to hire a private man to retrieve it by night. The fire captain refused unqualified entry and offered the later accompanied inventory process. Ownership mattered to what could be requested; it did not make a hot collapsing route safe for the person offering to walk it.

shoal_e12_relay_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_relay_05.text: The custodian who had rejected Yue's explanation yesterday nodded today without asking her to speak. Yue returned the nod and left the woman her own waiting. No dialogue had magically restored the eight drawings. The mould owners' relief did not obligate the record owners to forgive the relay's opportunity cost. Relationships could remain unsettled while people still used the same safe public space and respected its ordinary work boundary.

shoal_e12_relay_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_relay_06.text: Yue bought breakfast with her own received wages and rested in her paid lodging after the morning check. She had no technical task requiring her hand today. The ordinary practitioner had permitted walking with rest and prohibited more load handling until reassessed. She kept the restriction instead of disguising a pail as a smaller helpful object. Her sixth stage remained earned, and the changed body condition remained current.

shoal_e12_relay_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_relay_07.text: On Day Three Hundred Eleven, touch, grip, and leg checks returned to the previously permitted baseline under ordinary rest. The practitioner ended the temporary fingertip restriction within that narrow clearance and kept the old shoulder's overhead limit. Yue had observed recovery on a later date. She did not call herself healed of every weakness or volunteer to repeat the relay for an admiring audience. The next load would still need its actual conditions.

shoal_e12_relay_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_relay_08.text: Yan read the work clearance Yue permitted him to see and asked only whether she had understood its limits. She had. He accepted her decision to take no new emergency assignment. The current crew found other actual helpers under its staffed plan. Her stopped voluntary work could remain useful without continuing indefinitely. Thirty provisional moulds and four cracked pieces had reached custody; the annex loss remained a separate material fact.

shoal_e12_relay_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_relay_09.text: The mould worker who had cried beside the cart offered a cup of tea and no mould gift. He said he had slept badly because saved stock could still fail review. Yue accepted the tea and let him speak. Relief had been real yesterday, and uncertainty was real today. A surviving tool needed a current qualified condition before it could help a worker earn, which made the waiting more precise than a general announcement of salvage.

shoal_e12_relay_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_relay_10.text: She returned to the public updates without a pail, private record file, or current fingertip work restriction beyond her established narrow baseline. The two actual support-care slots were closed. Qualified review would establish the mould cart's real condition and the record cabinet's loss on later safe entry. Yue could listen to the larger containment account without turning a stopped useful interval into a claim that her body or the town had emerged unchanged.

shoal_e12_body_rejoin.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_body_rejoin.text: The public update concerned the current fire boundary and the occupied structures crews had protected. Yue stood outside the work lane with her own reported limits and no new assignment. The fire command had an actual night record, current relief crew, and known unanswered material questions. She waited while the captain unfolded the marked lane map, its paper smelling faintly of the place it described.

shoal_e12_contain_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_contain_01.text: By Day Three Hundred Eleven, the qualified crew had established a cooler outer lane and two protected occupied workrooms. Shed Six and the record-annex approach remained closed. The captain marked exactly where water, sand, ordinary separation, and relief labor had limited spread. The sea lay beyond those efforts, moving on its own. Yue could see why a distant observer might call the whole shoreline safe once the smoke thinned. The map made that claim too large.

shoal_e12_contain_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_contain_02.text: One owner asked for a seawall of qi before an offshore gust brought sparks back. Yue answered that her tested marker task supplied no such application. The captain did not wait for a spiritual solution. He assigned the available ordinary boats to move within their crews' current qualified mooring plans, kept combustible goods clear of exposed edges, and checked the upwind contact. The actual measures had limits; their value did not depend on pretending a cultivator could replace them.

shoal_e12_contain_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_contain_03.text: The boat crews had their own owners, wages, and competent hands. A fire command could request the offered movement and relay current hazard information; it could not seize a vessel for an unqualified rescue display. Two crews accepted the movement under their current conditions. A third boat was already beyond the affected berth and needed no new order. Its absence from the dramatic foreground did not make it secretly abandoned or waiting for Yue's attention.

shoal_e12_contain_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_contain_04.text: At the occupied net shop, workers had removed the particular dry stock nearest the exposed wall after the crew's current warning. Other goods remained inside under the owner's accepted plan. The fire had not touched that room. Its keeper complained about the interrupted repair trade and thanked the route hand in the same breath. Prevention could look like a needless inconvenience to anyone who expected danger to prove itself by crossing every protected threshold.

shoal_e12_contain_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_contain_05.text: The captain refused a request to spray water through every neighboring roof just in case. Unnecessary water could damage goods and weaken surfaces without improving the actual fire boundary. His crew applied its qualified judgment to present conditions, with its current equipment and people. The anxious requester wanted a more visible action. Yue understood the wish. Sometimes the smallest adequate measure looked inadequate because it did not resemble the disaster people had imagined.

shoal_e12_contain_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_contain_06.text: Yan checked the public path again after a relieving cart changed its corner. The familiar yesterday route now needed a different stool position. He moved the waiting mark before more people gathered. Yue stepped to the new side without treating each relocation as an insult. The crowd had begun to follow the ordinary command more readily after the roof fall. Fear had changed their cooperation. It had not made the path's physical width grow.

shoal_e12_contain_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_contain_07.text: At the care desk's public waiting area, the fourth rescued worker permitted a narrow update through his partner: a leg fracture had been stabilized, and he needed a longer ordinary assessment and rehabilitation plan. He was alive and not ready to resume his trade. The initial rescue count could therefore be complete while its bodily consequence remained serious. Yue heard the update only because the couple chose to offer it. Their private examination stayed with them.

shoal_e12_contain_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_contain_08.text: The couple's finite care deposit had an actual scope to discuss, not a blank promise of compensation. Thirty-two copper covered four workers' initial ordinary care scopes, forty was reserved for the fourth worker's accepted rehabilitation and support arrangement, eight for defined care travel, thirty for finite restricted-income support, and ten for ordinary dressings. The total was one hundred twenty. Spending would follow performed accepted care and actual receiving; a reserve line did not certify its future service already completed.

shoal_e12_contain_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_contain_09.text: The three other rescued workers had distinct injuries and restrictions. One chose to share a temporary smoke-exposure work limit, another a treated sleeve burn, and the third kept the clinical detail private. Their current earned wages remained governed by their employer's real terms. The care deposit did not buy every later canceled job. They could pursue applicable wage claims separately. Yue would not call the owner's finite funded care either a complete restoration or meaningless because it was incomplete.

shoal_e12_contain_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_contain_10.text: A displaced worker asked why the leg-injured man had an income-support line while her missed commissions did not. The receiver explained that this particular deposit's accepted emergency scope named rescued employees and finite restrictions. It did not settle her different trade loss. He gave the actual public claim channel without promising a new fund. Her anger at the distinction was understandable. An honestly bounded account could still reveal a town had no adequate answer for somebody else.

shoal_e12_contain_11.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_contain_11.text: He Ming collected offered public questions about those gaps, leaving private medical detail absent. His group had not become a universal representative by attending every meeting. One worker wanted him to speak; another declined because she planned to raise her own claim. He preserved both choices. Yue saw how an institution grew through such slow boundaries while urgent grief wanted a single person empowered to fix everything.

shoal_e12_contain_12.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_contain_12.text: Rong visited the public boundary with a revised delivery list. The unburned port freight-signal plates remained in their separate secured gallery, outside the affected shed and annex. Their six numbered transport crates had their own custody and future authorization process. He did not offer them as proof that the fire's other losses were minor. Their continued existence meant one later bounded journey could still be considered, not that a relay association's whole future had been saved by luck.

shoal_e12_contain_13.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_contain_13.text: The store steward asked to use that separate plate stock to compensate a mould owner. The port custodian refused because the two assets had different owners and purposes. A later properly approved transfer might be possible, but it had not been accepted here. Yue heard the refusal and recognized why surviving property needed its own rights even during grief. A visible intact resource was not automatically everybody's emergency purse.

shoal_e12_contain_14.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_contain_14.text: At the net shop, the younger brother from the quarantine meeting helped his sibling carry a permitted light bundle. He had not been a known worker inside the burning shed and had no fire injury to invent. Their earlier argument continued in fragments between ordinary tasks. The sibling thought the meeting had mattered; the brother thought its lost shift remained too costly. The town did not need every family disagreement resolved before people could help one another move a bundle.

shoal_e12_contain_15.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_contain_15.text: Song Mei's completed rehearsal interruption left its own missed room hour. The keeper offered a later replacement slot with different conditions, and she had not accepted it. She wanted a room where current loading would not cross the audience exit. Yue read the public offered time only when the artist showed it. The choice would belong to Song Mei. A performer could remain part of the town's recovery and decline to lend her voice to its preferred conclusion.

shoal_e12_contain_16.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_contain_16.text: The public fire-watch ledger recorded actual command changes, known receiving, and current closures. It was an ordinary operational record, not a cultivation chronicle. Yue's stage appeared only where her volunteered support body's limit had mattered to assignment. No clerk increased it to make the afternoon sound more impressive. The captain wanted a later reader to know who had worked, where the stop lay, and what the crew could no longer reach.

shoal_e12_contain_17.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_contain_17.text: During a quiet interval, a fire worker washed soot from his face at the public pump. He had missed his own meal while the first search continued, then eaten under the relief plan. He said the soup was cold and still the best thing he had tasted all day. Yue sat nearby after asking if company was welcome. They spoke about the soup rather than bravery. His ordinary appetite made the crew's labor feel more real than any phrase about tireless hands.

shoal_e12_contain_18.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_contain_18.text: The worker had been frightened when the roof shifted. He said that without apologizing. The prepared withdrawal route had allowed him to move instead of deciding in the instant whether fear meant cowardice. Yue remembered the supported release stroke and the independent stop. Different work needed different skills. Both could include a plan for the moment a person no longer felt certain. She did not ask him to compare his ordinary craft with her cultivation.

shoal_e12_contain_19.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_contain_19.text: A public requester wanted the fire-watch record copied immediately for a private sale. The keeper declined until its offered public extracts could be checked, with private people information excluded. That did not hide the visible disaster. The current alarm, closure, and care contacts were already posted. A fast sensational sheet might spread names and unverified counts farther than useful instructions. Song Mei's ownership of her fictional script had a different basis, but both refusals reminded Yue that circulation changed consequences.

shoal_e12_contain_20.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_contain_20.text: On Day Three Hundred Twelve, wind turned toward the cleared water edge. The fire crew adjusted its actual protection line and withdrew equipment from a hot support before it failed. Its collapse sent debris into an empty marked zone. No one stood there because the boundary had been checked. The lucky-looking result had ordinary work behind it, and the work could still fail elsewhere. Yue heard no proclamation that the crew had now mastered every possible collapse.

shoal_e12_contain_21.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_contain_21.text: The current smoke plume frightened passengers at a distant boarding quay. Their licensed crew checked the route and delayed boarding within its actual ordinary command. The delay would cost some connections, handled under those owners' applicable terms. It did not mean fire had reached their vessel. Sui's public contact distinguished a hazard precaution from a current affected structure. The difference gave people a way to ask the right operator before abandoning their road money in panic.

shoal_e12_contain_22.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_contain_22.text: A child at the public wall drew a roof with flames taller than the page. Another drew the pail line as a river of tiny cups. Their drawings could remember an event without certifying where every helper stood. Yue did not correct their art as though it were an operational record. The teacher wrote the children's offered date beneath each page and left their choices visible. There were other desks for factual counts.

shoal_e12_contain_23.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_contain_23.text: The teacher asked whether any public drawing could be displayed at the school. Each child and parent decided separately, and one family declined. Yue did not turn their refusal into a secret trauma explanation. They might simply want the drawing at home. The current town had room for grief kept private and art offered publicly. Both could exist beside a guarded wreck whose next safe entry had not yet been declared.

shoal_e12_contain_24.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_contain_24.text: At the clinic door, the potter showed Yue a newly altered grip on his tool. His practitioner had advised an ordinary current adjustment, and he had chosen to try it. It made one task easier without returning the unrelieved hours during the delayed supply week. He asked whether the fire's mould owners could use some of his spare plain supports later. She suggested he offer them directly under his own terms, not appoint her to distribute another person's generous idea.

shoal_e12_contain_25.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_contain_25.text: He did offer them, and two owners accepted particular supports after checking fit and their actual available work. Others declined because the shapes did not suit their tools. No one had to praise the offer as a solution to all lost moulds. The potter kept his unaccepted pieces. Generosity could support real new labor while leaving much of a destruction unresolved, which made it harder to announce and easier to trust.

shoal_e12_contain_26.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_contain_26.text: The public night command prepared another relief handover before darkness. It named known hot places, current isolated equipment, guarded approaches, and the next review time. Tired workers did not become invincible when the town called them heroes. They needed sleep and a successor who knew the actual present conditions. Yue watched the ordinary briefing and left before its private staff matters began, carrying a useful picture of an institution that could continue while particular people stopped.

shoal_e12_contain_27.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_contain_27.text: That evening, the private-tool owner stood near the guarded public gate and asked again when he could enter. The watch hand gave the actual current closure and later review time. He had heard both before. He wanted a different answer because the tools were his father's and his own work had sharpened them for years. Yue recognized him from the fire rope. She stopped outside the active lane when he called her name.

shoal_e12_contain_28.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_contain_28.text: He asked whether she had ever made anything that somebody else could declare unreachable. Yue said she knew the tools mattered and could not authorize entry. He pointed at the gate as if her refusal had built it. The ordinary watch hand was speaking to another owner a few steps away. Yue should have ended the conversation there. Instead, she tried to explain the hot support and later accompanied inventory once more, hoping a clearer sentence would make his anger safer.

shoal_e12_contain_29.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_contain_29.text: The man stepped close and caught her sleeve above the elbow. Yue turned to free it without loading her old shoulder beyond its clearance. He shoved from the side before she had a stable ordinary stance. Her hip struck the low boundary post, and she fell onto the hard public stone with her elbow under her. No qi shield appeared. She had misjudged his movement and her position. Six opened primary pairs did not correct that mistake in the instant.

shoal_e12_contain_30.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_contain_30.text: The watch hand reached them and restrained the man under the current ordinary public procedure. Yan moved bystanders out of the route and called for qualified care. Yue could hear the tool owner still shouting that they had ruined his living. His loss was real, and his hand had caused a separate harm. Neither fact replaced the other. She stayed seated where the care worker directed, with a sharp ache running from the elbow into her forearm.

shoal_e12_contain_31.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_contain_31.text: A child began to cry at the sight of the fall. His parent led him away before he could become part of a public accusation. The watch hand recorded the people who offered an actual view. Yue had seen the man approach and felt the shove; another person had seen the side movement more clearly. She gave her narrow account when able. She did not invent a complete angle because the injury was hers.

shoal_e12_contain_32.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_contain_32.text: At the ordinary clinical desk, Yue paid the current four-copper assessment fee from her own received wages. The already closed support-care allowance was not reopened. The practitioner examined the elbow, checked touch, grip, leg stability, and other reported symptoms, and found a bruise without an observed fracture in the current ordinary assessment. He warned her which changes required immediate return. He stopped powered and load work pending actual follow-up, with the old shoulder restriction still intact.

shoal_e12_contain_33.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_contain_33.text: The assessment's advice did not erase the pain or certify every hidden condition impossible. Yue could walk with rest and attend ordinary public receiving, but would not carry pails, lift return stock, or conduct a powered trial. The next review was set for Day Three Hundred Fourteen, with another on Three Hundred Twenty-One if needed by the current course. She accepted those dates without scheduling a private practice to prove the fall had changed nothing.

shoal_e12_contain_34.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_contain_34.text: The watch receiver asked whether she wanted her offered injury account recorded with the current assault report. She did. The man would answer through the ordinary process, separate from his lawful lost-tool claim. He could still request a later accompanied inventory; he could not enter hot debris or strike a person because his request had been refused. Yue had no authority to decide his punishment at the clinic desk and did not ask her cultivation certificate to make the decision larger.

shoal_e12_contain_35.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_contain_35.text: Her embarrassment hurt almost as much as the elbow. She had not lost a duel against a magnificent enemy. She had fallen at a public post after misreading an angry ordinary man. The clinician told her embarrassment was not a reason to load the arm while it was restricted. Yue laughed once and regretted the motion when the bruise pulled. A body could be ridiculous and injured together, without either condition making the other less real.

shoal_e12_contain_36.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_contain_36.text: Yan came to ask whether her account and care receiving were complete. He did not say she should have been able to defeat the man at sixth stage. He asked why she had stayed close after the gate's answer was clear. Yue said she had wanted him to hear it from somebody he knew. Yan said that was understandable and had not worked. They let the plain failure sit between them without inventing an instant lesson that made the bruise worthwhile.

shoal_e12_contain_37.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_contain_37.text: The tool owner was held through the ordinary current watch process. His relatives were given the applicable public contact, not permission to bargain with Yue's medical details. One asked the keeper whether a public apology would erase the report. The keeper said the injured person's account and the actual procedure were not a fee to be exchanged for a better speech. The relatives went to speak with the proper desk. The burned tools remained behind the fire boundary.

shoal_e12_contain_38.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_contain_38.text: Song Mei learned of the incident through Yue's offered message rather than public clinical gossip. She came at a time Yue accepted and brought ordinary food bought from her own money. The artist looked angry when she saw the supported arm. Yue asked her not to make the man into a monster in a verse. Song Mei said she had not asked to write a verse and wanted to know whether Yue had eaten.

shoal_e12_contain_39.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_contain_39.text: They shared the food at the keeper's permitted table. Song Mei complained that people kept expecting her to turn every bad event into something they could applaud. Yue admitted she had expected a comforting sentence from a performer who knew how to end a story. The artist said this one did not need an ending tonight. It needed the meal, the actual restriction, and enough sleep. Her voice was tired rather than beautifully wise.

shoal_e12_contain_40.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_contain_40.text: Yue told her about the instant of wanting a clearer sentence to stop the man. Song Mei asked whether he had been unable to understand or unwilling to accept. Yue thought he had understood. Saying that made the failure different. It had not been a language task she could complete by better wording. She had remained close to someone choosing aggression. The ordinary watch could act after it began, but could not undo the physical moment.

shoal_e12_contain_41.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_contain_41.text: Song Mei stayed for the agreed short visit and then left for her own lodging. She did not move into Yue's room or promise to supervise every future conversation. Yue appreciated the ordinary goodbye because it kept care from becoming another indefinite role. The bruise still hurt when she tried to pull the coat over its elbow. She asked the keeper's offered light assistance and paid for no hidden extra service beyond what was actually agreed.

shoal_e12_contain_42.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_contain_42.text: On Day Three Hundred Thirteen, Yue woke with the elbow still tender. The practitioner's listed urgent warning signs had not appeared by her own report, but the current restriction remained until review. She attended the public fire update without a load or powered task. The supported arm made walking slower because she avoided crowding and sudden turns. Her body carried a new condition through the town, making her avoid sudden crowded turns and learn which ordinary small tasks needed help.

shoal_e12_contain_43.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_contain_43.text: The watch report preserved the offered witnesses and current injury receiving. It did not publish the private clinical details Yue had withheld. The man had a scheduled ordinary hearing under the applicable process and no authority to force a hot-site entry while waiting. His relatives asked for the current lawful loss inventory time. The fire keeper gave it. A person could be responsible for aggression and still retain property rights the town had to handle properly.

shoal_e12_contain_44.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_contain_44.text: At the guarded wreck, the qualified crew found heat lower but several supports still unstable. The captain opened only a specified outside review lane, not the inside stock rooms. Owners could observe marks from the safe boundary and submit their location information. Yue's bruised elbow gave her no privileged entry, and her sixth-stage history gave no immunity from debris. She listened from the public side while ordinary qualified workers continued the final safe-access preparation.

shoal_e12_contain_45.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_contain_45.text: The record and mould owners waited under their actual selected custody states. Surviving material had its named keeper; burned or inaccessible material had its pending qualified inventory. A rumor claimed everything had been saved because no known worker died inside. The captain corrected it publicly. Rescue and material preservation were different counts. The fourth worker's fractured leg also remained a bodily cost despite his survival. Nobody needed to die for the afternoon's losses to be real.

shoal_e12_contain_46.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_contain_46.text: The known injured worker and his partner accepted a current rehabilitation discussion for the next day, under the finite care deposit. The discussion would choose actual sessions and travel rather than promise a perfect leg. Yue heard the offered public time and kept her own clinical review separate. Their care belonged to them, with ordinary professionals and accepted funding. Her new bruise did not give her authority to compare whose pain deserved the greater sympathy.

shoal_e12_contain_47.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_contain_47.text: Rong brought a current supplier statement that named his unburned goods and the separate affected owner stock accurately. He wanted customers to know which orders could still proceed. The public clerk required the statement to leave uncertain losses uncertain until inventory. He accepted the change after arguing about how much uncertainty would cost. A correct commercial account could be hard to sell. That difficulty did not justify assigning a surviving asset to replace one the owner actually lacked.

shoal_e12_contain_48.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_contain_48.text: He Ming's group prepared a later public question about the store movement after the lamp check. They would need the actual witnesses, dates, and permissions, not the conclusion that an earlier inspection must prove someone guilty. Yue could offer her own outside account and the publicly available rag-flare record. The inside lamp spill belonged to its witnesses. Her injured arm would keep her from an assigned handling task, not from thinking carefully about what she had seen.

shoal_e12_contain_49.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_contain_49.text: At the clinic's public door, the potter saw the supported arm and asked whether the cup's bad foot had finally attacked. Yue laughed carefully. He listened to the offered brief account and stopped before asking for private treatment details. Then he said his imperfect cup would not apologize either. The joke gave her a moment in which injury was ordinary company rather than public proof of a cultivator's surprising vulnerability.

shoal_e12_contain_50.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_contain_50.text: The potter offered to carry her bought bread along the permitted route while he walked that way himself. Yue accepted the light assistance and did not turn it into a new paid escort job. He left at his own workshop door as before. The apprentice had a current kiln question waiting. Ordinary friendships could contain such exact endings and still feel warm. Her restricted arm did not require every helpful person to become an attendant.

shoal_e12_contain_51.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_contain_51.text: That evening, the fire captain declared the exterior safe-access preparation complete for the specified next-day qualified inventory. Hot inside pockets and unstable marked supports remained excluded. The closure map carried both usable and forbidden paths, each with its current review condition. Owners would meet the responsible reader and crew at the stated time. The fire had been contained within finite ordinary effort, leaving a wreck that now needed careful facts instead of heroic promises.

shoal_e12_contain_52.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_contain_52.text: Yue put her own clinical receipt beside the next-day review time, then set it apart from the property-inventory invitation. Both belonged to Day Three Hundred Fourteen and had different authorities. She could attend each only within its actual hour and her current body limit. The borrowed or private assets from Lark remained settled; none would reappear to solve an elbow bruise or inspect burned wood. She slept with the arm supported as advised, while the guarded site waited for daylight.

shoal_e12_contain_53.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_contain_53.text: By morning, surviving owners would learn the condition of what had reached lawful storage, and losing owners would learn what the qualified wreck inventory could actually confirm. The difference had begun with Yue's support choice under smoke and a crew's finite safe routes. It would not become a measure of her cultivation. She wanted to hear the facts because people needed them to choose new work, not because a clean final tally could forgive every part of the fire.

shoal_e12_private_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_private_01.text: Before closing her eyes, Yue tried to write a account of the afternoon that did not sound like a public witness statement. She wrote that she had been afraid, then crossed out an explanation that made fear admirable. She had also been annoyed at the keeper's closing hour and grateful for the potter's joke. Those feelings did not require a receiving state. She could keep a page whose purpose was simply to tell herself what the day had felt like.

shoal_e12_private_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_private_02.text: She wrote that the tool owner had understood the gate's answer and chosen to shove her anyway. Then she wrote that he had lost tools she could not restore. Keeping both sentences felt harder than choosing which one should explain the man. Neither sentence asked her to forgive him before the ordinary process did its work. Neither erased the steel he might still find among the wreck under qualified entry.

shoal_e12_private_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e12_private_03.text: The private page ended without an elegant last line. Yue left space below it for tomorrow rather than making an injury teach the exact lesson she wanted. The current clinical advice gave enough direction for tonight: support the arm, rest, return on the specified signs or at review. She followed it and let a ordinary evening end. Beyond the window, the harbor's night watch called its current hour to people whose own stories were still awake.
